objective: Add provider-neutral fail-closed task-level routing leases that pin one selected backend across a bounded multi-turn task trace, enforce sequence/generation/expiry/replay fences, and accept delayed terminal outcome evidence without invoking models or granting authority.

research_inputs.finding: Computer-use systems should isolate execution, retain human oversight for high-impact actions, and treat screenshots, page text, tool outputs, PDFs, emails, chats, and third-party content as untrusted input.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Task routing receipts remain evidence-only and do not authorize tools, browser actions, external side effects, or model-generated permissions.

research_inputs.finding: Agent accountability requires provenance connecting tools, memory, observations, claims, actions, and agent interactions rather than relying only on final-answer accuracy.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Leases bind task context, route evidence, turn request digests, terminal trace, terminal outcome evidence, and delayed feedback state.

research_inputs.finding: TRACE-Router identifies request-level routing as misaligned with long-horizon agent tasks because quality feedback is observed only at task termination; sticky task-level assignment improves credit-assignment coherence and preserves model-specific state across a trace.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds a bounded task lease that pins one selected endpoint for all turns and records terminal quality/latency evidence without changing the existing request-level router.

features: single backend pin across bounded multi-turn trace
terminal quality and latency delayed-feedback receipt

real_task.multi_turn_trace: 3 turns admitted to one pinned backend and terminal delayed feedback completed

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane receipt overhead; excludes model calls, provider routing, network, memory, accelerator, and kernel scheduling latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the task-routing module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged intervention release

limitations: The contract pins evidence to a backend but does not invoke models or guarantee that an external runtime honors the pin.
Terminal quality and latency are caller-supplied observations and do not independently prove model quality or task correctness.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes actual model inference, network, KV-cache, accelerator, and kernel scheduler behavior.
The real-task validation uses a deterministic local multi-turn fixture and does not establish general intelligence, browser autonomy, robotics, or production agent efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
